blocks.text: The opening heading presents these sayings as proverbs of Solomon copied or transcribed by officials of Hezekiah, king of Judah. It also places this chapter within a book that explicitly preserves distinct collections and voices, rather than presenting every proverb as part of one undifferentiated sequence.

Verses 21–22 command practical care for an enemy, then speak of heaping coals of fire on the enemy’s head. The precise force of that image is debated. A later use of these verses in Romans 12 places them within a rejection of private vengeance and a call to blessing, peace, and overcoming evil with good; the saying therefore cannot be read as permission for concealed retaliation.
